repositories.name: ZhuLinsen/patchloop

inspected_code.finding: Separates hard rejection reasons from approval reasons. Explicit commands and owner-authored non-feature tasks can supply authorisation; features retain separate handling. Blocked paths and publish-target policy are separate checks. Tests cover these distinctions.

Task claims record lease_owner, attempt count and start time. Failures move to retry_waiting or dead_letter; running tasks can be recovered. State uses an instance-local threading.Lock and temporary-file os.replace persistence.
Queue wrapper exposes enqueue, claim, success, failure, retry and recovery, with bounded attempts by default. This makes recovery behaviour an explicit contract.

repositories.atlas_boundary: Useful design for Maintenance50, but the inspected JSON state store is not a demonstrated multi-process coordinator. Independently running agents must not share it without transactional claims, owner checks/fencing and competing-worker tests. No claim that50workers or production safety were validated.

repositories.name: ZhuLinsen/MiniAgent
repositories.purpose: Alpha agent harness with replaceable loop, plugins, managed tools and resumable sessions.

inspected_code.finding: Agent loop has a maximum step count, rejects missing/reused tool-call IDs, requires object arguments and records tool-start events. If a non-read tool raises after starting, it records uncertain effects and stops for inspection rather than blindly continuing.
Rejects duplicate tools; validates parameter JSON Schema at registration and arguments before execution, then authorises through Policy before the executor runs.

Defines readonly/confirm/trusted modes, resolves managed file paths inside a workspace and restricts sensitive file patterns. Its docstring expressly states that arbitrary shell/plugins are not isolated.

repositories.atlas_boundary: Adopt the tool-state contract and test with a fake backend. Permission checks and plugin hooks must not be represented as an operating-system sandbox.

repositories.name: ZhuLinsen/FastDatasets

inspected_code.finding: Carries chunk_id, file, content and summary into generated question records; tracks answer failures and filters error-marked samples before returning the dataset. This retains useful source lineage, but generated answers are not independent evidence of truth.

Static empty-generation failure: if chunks are nonempty but all question-generation calls yield[], total_questions=0 and batch_size=0, then total_batches divides by batch_size at line234. Add an explicit zero-question outcome instead of allowing a crash. Not executed against an LLM.

TextSplitter uses headings and sentence boundaries with nominal min/max lengths. A single sentence longer than max_len can append an empty chunk then retain the oversized sentence, so max_len is not a proven hard bound. Test long punctuation-free input before reuse.

repositories.atlas_boundary: For legal/research training examples, preserve source hashes and pinpoint spans, quarantine generated suggestions, reject empty/error outputs and keep validation cases separate from training. Do not present synthetic answers as verified scholarship.

strongest_trial.name: Commit-bound review receipt replay
strongest_trial.target: Existing Atlas Maintenance 50 review workflow and Opsbook fixtures
strongest_trial.scope: Use local mocked PR/check snapshots to produce ready, failed, pending, missing-check, changed-head and nonconvergent outcomes. Begin without network access or automatic posting/merging.
strongest_trial.acceptance: A push invalidates the old receipt; an absent required check and an empty check list cannot pass; repeated regressions on previously edited lines stop within the declared round budget.
strongest_trial.policy_difference: Upstream code classifies neutral checks as passing and skipped checks separately. Atlas must define its required-check policy explicitly instead of inheriting those defaults silently.
